newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 7.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The railway workers union will continue to strike for another 24 hours. According to the chairman of the union, Jaromir Dusek, the union extended the strike because the Transport Ministry did not guarantee to fulfill the union's requests, which they presented on the first day of the strike.

- The cabinet has five days to inform parliament of steps that it plans to take to ensure that hospitals are not weighed down by enormous debts. According to Vice-chairman of Parliament Petra Buzkova, the total owed by all hospitals under the administration of the Health Ministry amounted to 1.73 billion crowns by September 30 last year.

- Despite an impressive start during the first half of last year for industrial output, it slowed considerably in the last quarter of the year. Although full-year production growth was originally estimated at around 10 percent, according to reports released yesterday from the Czech Statistical Bureau, year-on-year growth amounted to 6.9 percent.

PRAVO - Ceska Zbrojovka Uhersky Brod supplied Turkish police with 100,000 CZ 75 calibre 9 mm Luger pistols, according to a spokesman for the munitions factory, Jiri Frenzl. He added that the Turks have placed an order for more guns, which should be finalised in March and April.
- At the end of January, daily output of the new model Skoda Octavia amounted to 60 automobiles. By summer, Skoda Mlada Boleslav expects to reach its goal of making 400 Octavias daily.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Nearly 26 percent of schools and approximately 40 percent of school workers participated in the third day of the chain strike in the districts of Tabor, Bruntal, Ceskobudejovice, Pisek, Breclav and Jicin organised by the largest school workers union CMOS. The amount of participants in the strike is gradually decreasing.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Losses caused to railways due to the current strike reached at least 0.5 billion crowns by midnight last night according to various economists and officials. This sum will most probably be repaid by taxpayers.
